messages:
sarah: FYI Acme support ticket — after canarying model v11.2 some of their function calls are failing with schema errors and strange auth drops, plus a billing spike.
kevin: can you paste the failing request/response and any gateway logs?
sarah: pasted from customer and our gateway traces:
```
POST /v1/exec
Headers: Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***, x-customer-id: acme-123
body: {"model":"redwood-v11.2","input":"...","tools":[{"name":"send_email " ,"args":{"to":"ops@acme.com","user_id":null}}]}
RESP 400 {"error":"tool_validation_failed","details":"missing required field 'user_id'"}
Gateway: 502 from tool-resolver, then retry -> 200 but routed to legacy-email-plugin (billing cost x4)
```
maria: I see p95 latency jump on /v1/exec around 18:10 UTC during the canary, matches resolver retry spike.
kevin: interesting: the tool name in the payload has a trailing space: "send_email ". Did v11.2 change tool metadata normalization? That could make the selector miss exact matches.
sarah: customer says they didn’t change anything client-side. They report ~20% of calls 400, another portion succeed, and client retries push traffic to legacy plugin which bills more.
luis: ops-bot flagged Authorization header missing in ~13% of failing traces between gateway and resolver. If fallback path uses a proxy that drops auth, that could explain missing token-derived user binding causing schema rejects.
ops-bot: alert: route /exec resolver-retries spike at 2026-03-16T18:09:21Z, error_rate 6.1% (+4.5%)
kevin: hypothesis: v11.2 emits tool names with extra whitespace or non-ascii whitespace chars; our resolver does exact-match lookup so it falls back to legacy alias with a different schema that enforces user_id.
maria: I pulled resolver input blobs, confirmed cases where "tool_name":"send_email \u200B" (zero-width) or trailing ASCII space vs canonical "send_email". Also spotted a reserialization step that drops keys with null values, so user_id:null -> removed -> schema validation fails.
sarah: repro steps from customer: 1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exec -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"redwood-v11.2","prompt":"send invoice", "tools": ... }' 2) ~1/5 calls -> 400 tool_validation_failed 3) retries -> some calls routed to legacy-email-plugin -> charged ~0.12 USD/token vs expected ~0.03
kevin: I'll run an internal canary-sim run: 10k requests -> 19% resolver mismatches, and in all mismatches I see trailing or invisible unicode whitespace in tool_name.
maria: confirmed header-drop: our resolver-fallback proxy has a branch that uses a different upstream client which doesn't copy Authorization when the selector was a fuzzy match. That's a bug.
luis: impact summary: Acme experienced partial failures, elevated p95 latency (+120ms), and a billing multiplier due to retries. They're escalated.
sarah: recommended immediate mitigation: 1) pause v11.2 canary 2) enforce strict no-legacy-fallback for canary traffic 3) offer billing credit and notify customer. Can we rollback the canary now?
kevin: initiating rollback to v11.1 canary in 3m. Also will prepare a hotfix: trim/unicode-normalize tool names in resolver and ensure Authorization preserved on all fallback proxied calls.
maria: I'll add a temporary proxy guard: preserve Authorization header always, and short-circuit to fail-fast on non-exact tool-name matches to avoid hitting legacy plugin.
ops-bot: deploy-started: rollback redwood-v11.2 canary -> v11.1 at 2026-03-16T18:21:00Z by kevin.
kevin: rollback running — monitoring telemetry.
kevin: rollback complete. p95 latency returned to baseline, resolver-mismatch rate dropped to <0.1%.
sarah: I notified Acme: v11.2 canary rolled back, investigating root cause (trailing/invisible whitespace in tool metadata + fallback proxy auth bug), will credit billing overage and follow up with timeline.
luis: created ticket PRO-4532 for hotfix: normalize tool names + preserve auth on fallback. Assigned kevin/maria. Finance to process credit for Acme.
kevin: working on PR to trim unicode whitespace and normalize case in resolver lookup; adding unit/integration fuzz tests injecting invisible chars.
sarah: closing the immediate support escalation; customer accepted rollback and temporary credit. Keeping PRO-4532 open until hotfix and re-canary plan.
maria: scheduling a short postmortem and adding checklist items: canary selector exact-match tests, fallback auth invariant, billing regen & customer-impact validation.
kevin: followups: add a harness that mutates tool names (ASCII/non-ASCII whitespace, casing) to ensure resolver mapping is resilient.
sarah: thanks all :thumbsup: I'll add notes to incident runbook and update the customer thread with the credit confirmation.
